5.6.7 Rte_Invalidate Purpose: Invalidate a data element for an “explicit” sender-receiver transmis- sion. Signature: [SWS_Rte_01206] Upstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00310, SRS_Rte_00078 ⌈ If returnValueProvision of the related dataSendPoint(s) is not set to noReturnValueProvided: Std_ReturnType Rte_[Byps_]Invalidate_

_( [IN Rte_Instance ], [OUT Std_TransformerError transformerError]) If returnValueProvision of the related dataSendPoint(s) is set to noReturnValueProvided: void Rte_[Byps_]Invalidate_

_( [IN Rte_Instance ], [OUT Std_TransformerError transformerError]) Where

is the port name and the VariableDataPro- totype within the sender-receiver interface categorizing the port. [Byps_] is an optional infix used when component wrapper method for bypass support is enabled for the related software component type.⌋ Existence: [SWS_Rte_01282] Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00051, SRS_Rte_00078 ⌈An Rte_Invalidate API shall be created for any VariableAc- cess in the dataSendPoint role that references a provided Vari- ableDataPrototype which associated InvalidationPolicy is set to keep, replace or externalReplacement.⌋ [SWS_Rte_CONSTR_09018] Rte_Invalidate API may only be used by the runnable that describe its usage ⌈The Rte_Inval- idate API may only be used by the runnable that contains the cor- responding VariableAccess in the dataSendPoint role⌋ [SWS_Rte_08582] Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00249 ⌈The optional OUT parameter transformerError of the API shall be generated if the PortPrototype of port

is referenced by a PortAPIOption which has the attribute errorHandling set to transformerErrorHandling.⌋ Description: The Rte_Invalidate API takes the instance handle as input pa- rameter. The return value is used to indicate the success, or other- wise, of the API call to the caller. The OUT parameter transformerError contains the transformer error which occured during execution of the transformer chain. See chapter 4.10.5. Return Val…
